arabic text: O my Asgher, where are you? Come your mother is calling\nfor you -- Banu is weeping, O my baby
english translation text: O my Asghar, where are you? Come—your mother is calling you.\nBano is weeping, O my baby.

arabic text: The skies are darkening, the desert is cold\nGone is my baby just six months old (´2)\nI cannot find him, my little prince
english translation text: The skies are darkening and the desert has grown cold.\nMy six-month-old baby is gone.\nI cannot find him, my little prince.

arabic text: You were so thirsty, your tongue was so dry\nWe couldn’t fetch you water though we did try (´2)\nIs your thirst quenched now? O beloved one
english translation text: You were so thirsty, and your tongue was so dry.\nWe could not bring you water, though we tried.\nIs your thirst now quenched, O beloved one?

arabic text: When Hurmala aimed his arrow at you\nDid he know that he would hurt me too? \nMy heart is broken, O where are you?
english translation text: When Hurmala aimed his arrow at you,\ndid he know he would wound me too? \nMy heart is broken—where are you?

arabic text: My lap is empty now, your cradle is bare\nI cannot find you anywhere (´2)\nWho will I rock now? My precious son
english translation text: My lap is empty now, and your cradle lies bare.\nI cannot find you anywhere.\nWhom will I rock now, my precious son?

arabic text: How can I leave you in Kerbala?\nThe youngest martyr on Ashura (´2)\nHow can my baby sleep in the sand?
english translation text: How can I leave you in Karbala,\nthe youngest martyr of Ashura? \nHow can my baby sleep beneath the sand?

arabic text: How can I go back to Medina?\nWhat will I say to your sister Sughra? (´2)\nWhat will I do now my Asgher is gone?
english translation text: How can I return to Madina?\nWhat will I tell your sister Sughra? \nWhat will I do now that my Asghar is gone?
